Best Vegan Protein Bars - Ranking 262 Bars by Ingredient Quality

We checked 1,298 protein bars available in the US for whey, milk, honey, egg, collagen, casein, and gelatin. The result: 262 bars, about 20%, have none of them. We rank the best vegan protein bars by ingredient quality, brand, and macros. Not just us telling you the flavors we like.

What disqualifies a protein bar from being vegan

We mark a bar vegan only when the full ingredient list has zero animal-derived ingredients, not just when the package says "plant-based." The 7 ingredients below are the ones we screen for, in order of how often they show up.

1,036 of the 1,298 bars we track, 80%, are not vegan. Whey protein alone accounts for more disqualified bars than any other single ingredient. Combined, these 7 ingredients account for 754 of the 1036 non-vegan bars (72.8%); the rest use some other animal-derived ingredient further down the label.

The default protein source in most mainstream bars, usually listed as whey protein isolate or concentrate near the top of the ingredient list.

What we found screening 1,298 bars

80%
of protein bars are not vegan
1,036 of 1,298 bars we track use an animal-derived ingredient somewhere in the formula. Whey protein alone shows up in more bars than any other single animal ingredient we screen for.
Pea protein is the plant-protein default.
125 of the 262 vegan bars use pea protein, more than soy protein (48) and brown rice protein (50) combined.
Larabar and GoMacro do not bother with a whey version.
Larabar (29 flavors) and GoMacro (17 flavors) are entirely vegan, more than any other brand we track. Both build around dates, nuts, and rice or pea protein rather than an isolate.
Vegan bars trade protein for fiber and a slightly cleaner score.
Vegan bars average 9.9g of protein against a database-wide average of 13.2g, but they carry more fiber (5.2g vs. 5.0g) and a slightly higher average ingredient score (5.2 vs. 4.6).
Being vegan and being clean are different questions.
The 4 Barebells flavors that clear the vegan screen grade D to F, while grade has nothing to do with animal ingredients. A vegan label does not guarantee a clean ingredient list.
NuGo splits closer to even than any other brand.
20 of NuGo's 30 flavors are vegan, the rest built on whey or milk protein instead. It is the largest genuinely mixed lineup in the database.
70.2% of vegan bars grade A or B.
That beats the database-wide rate of 56.7%. Whole-food brands like Larabar and GoMacro pull the vegan average up.

Frequently asked questions

We mark a bar vegan when its ingredient list has zero animal-derived ingredients, cross-checked against the full label, not just a package claim. That means no whey, milk protein, honey, egg whites, collagen peptides, casein, or gelatin anywhere in the formula.
262 of the 1,298 bars we track are vegan, spanning 46 brands. 55 of those 262 bars grade A for ingredient quality.
Yes. All 29 Larabar flavors we track are vegan. Larabar builds its bars around dates, nuts, and fruit rather than a dairy or egg-based protein source.
Yes. All 17 GoMacro flavors we track are vegan, built on organic brown rice protein rather than whey or milk protein.
A few. 4 of Barebells' 25 flavors are vegan, and those 4 grade D to F for ingredient quality, worse than the brand's non-vegan lineup. Being vegan and having a clean ingredient list are two different questions here.
Whey protein. It shows up in 523 of the 1,298 bars we track, more than milk protein, honey, collagen, casein, egg whites, and gelatin individually. It is the default protein source for most mainstream bars.
No. Honey is produced by bees, not a plant, so any bar listing honey as an ingredient does not qualify as vegan on this site, even if every other ingredient is plant-based.
Yes, and it is common. NuGo splits closest to even of any brand we checked: 20 of 30 flavors are vegan. Always check the specific flavor, not just the brand.
262 bars across 46 brands clear our vegan screen, led by whole-food brands like Larabar and GoMacro that qualify 100% of the time. The full ranked list is in the table below, sorted by ingredient quality.
1,036 of the 1,298 bars we track contain an animal-derived ingredient. Whey protein is the single biggest reason, followed by milk protein, honey, and collagen peptides.
No. Vegan bars in our database average a slightly higher ingredient quality score than the database as a whole, and carry more fiber. What they give up on average is protein: vegan bars average 9.9g against a database-wide average well above that, since whey and milk protein are calorie-for-calorie easier to pack into a bar than plant protein.
We update the database whenever new bars are added or a brand reformulates. Manufacturers do change their ingredient lists over time, so always confirm against the packaging in front of you. This page reflects the database as of 2026-08-31.
